finding: Row 11's named mutant survives row 11, and I replayed it rather than reading it. The row asserts four convergence numbers and names as its mutant 'count the streak as a total rather than a trailing run', justified by 'v0.35.0 has three clean-under-blocking rounds before round 3'. Replaying the committed corpus (spec/.tp-review/0.35.0 and 0.36.0, 22 audit-round-*.ndjson files) under both counting rules gives identical results in all eight cells the row pins: v0.35.0 blocking 3/3, all 9/9; at audit_clean_rounds 1, 2/2 and 8/8; v0.36.0 blocking 3/3, all never/never. The reason is structural, not a fixture accident — a total and a trailing run first reach k at the same round, because they can only diverge after a clean round has already been followed by an unclean one, which is past the first convergence. The justification is also arithmetically impossible: only rounds 1 and 2 precede round 3, round 1 carries two error rows, so there is exactly ONE clean-under-blocking round before round 3, not three. §7's own preamble says every row 'names the mutant that must fail it'; the only row guarding §2.1 — the section that decides the release's default — names one that passes.
suggestion: Replace the mutant with one that actually reddens the numbers. Two that do: grade a non-PASS row with no usable severity as advisory (v0.35.0 round 4's rows carry error, so misgrading absent severity moves nothing, but the unrecognised fixtures of row 8 do) or, on the streak itself, 'treat a round with no non-PASS rows as clean under blocking WITHOUT checking severity' — which leaves all/blocking identical and reddens the blocking column in both cycles. Delete the 'three clean-under-blocking rounds' clause; the number is one.

finding: Row 19's prescribed replacement clause introduces exactly the word §2 refuses and the mechanism §5 declines. Rows 2 and 3 of §6 must be rewritten to say convergence counts every non-PASS row 'the resolved policy does not accept', and engine.DivergenceHint is a shipped constant that skills/tp/REFERENCE.md quotes verbatim, so that sentence ships to every operator. §2 explicitly rejects the synonym on this exact ground: 'Surviving is deliberately not the word: it would imply a disposition that removes a row from the count, which §5 declines to create.' 'Accept' implies the same disposition more strongly, because tp already ships a command that looks like it: `tp audit <file> --resolve <role>:<item> wontfix <reason>` runs today (internal/cli/audit_signal_test.go:480 exercises it), writes a `resolved` key on the row, and TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate exists precisely to prove that disposition does NOT stop the row counting. A reader of the new hint will conclude it does. §2's next_action table and §7 row 10 carry the same word ('accepted rows', 'the accepted count'), so the collision is release-wide rather than one sentence.
suggestion: Name the policy instead of a per-row verb: 'audit convergence counts every non-PASS row under audit_converge_on: all, and every row carrying a blocking severity under blocking.' That is true under both values, names the field so the reader can act, and cannot be read as a disposition. Apply the same substitution to §2's table cells and row 10 ('the count of open non-PASS rows in the round').

finding: §2 says the field is refused at the consuming sink 'on the same terms as review_converge_on', and row 3 pins that as an exit code. Measured, the two paths are not on the same terms and the difference is ordering, not wording. Built /tmp/tp-dev/tp from this tree and ran both sinks over identical trees whose task file stores an invalid converge value: `tp review spec.md --record f.ndjson` exits 1 and leaves NO .tp-review state at all — it resolves and validates before writing; `tp audit spec.md --record a.ndjson` exits 0, and .tp-review/spec/state.json holds round 1 with clean:false and the round file on disk. Reading internal/cli/audit_record.go shows why: `clean := findings == 0` is line 71, `recordAuditRoundEntry(..., findings, clean, ...)` is line 85, and `engine.ResolveWorkflow` is line 91 — the audit record path resolves the workflow AFTER the round is stored and validates this class of field nowhere. This release makes `clean` a function of the resolved policy, so the resolve must move above line 71; but row 3 asserts only an exit code, so an implementation that leaves the order alone and validates at line 91 passes row 3 while having already written a round whose clean byte was stamped under no policy. §2 makes that permanent — stamping is record-time and the only undo it names is 're-records the round', which appends.
suggestion: State in §2 that the audit record path resolves and validates audit_converge_on BEFORE it computes clean and before recordAuditRoundEntry, so a refused --record writes no round — the property tp review --record already has. Extend row 3's audit half to assert it: after the refused invocation the state directory is byte-identical (no new round entry, no new audit-round-N.ndjson).

finding: §4's closing invariant — 'error + unrecognised sums the round's blocking rows and the two sections cannot drift apart' — is asserted over two different populations, and both are in this release. §4's buckets run in `--merge`'s summary loop, which internal/cli/audit_merge.go:64 iterates over `unique`, the set after dedupAuditRows removed (role,item_id) duplicates. §2's blocking predicate runs at the record sink over the recorded file's rows, and internal/cli/audit_record.go's countAuditFindings walks every non-blank line of that file with no dedup at all. They agree only when the operator records exactly the bytes --merge emitted; --record accepts any NDJSON path, and duplicates_removed is non-zero often enough that --merge reports it as a headline field. So a round recorded from the unmerged concatenation blocks on a duplicate error row that §4's breakdown counts once — the two sections drift by construction, in the direction that makes the emitted breakdown understate the gate.
suggestion: Scope the invariant to the population: 'over the rows --merge emitted, error + unrecognised equals the number of rows §2's predicate treats as blocking.' Then say in §2 that the record sink's predicate runs over the recorded file's rows as countAuditFindings walks them, deduplicated or not, so the two sections are comparable only when --record is fed --merge's output — which is the documented order, not a guarantee.

finding: §6 makes the sweep the deliverable rather than the count — the right move — but then gives no way to run it or to tell when it is done. The predicate is four semantic kinds ((a) states what audit convergence counts, (b) promises clean/next_action/--check unchanged, (c) says tp has no audit-side equivalent, (d) enumerates the settable workflow fields) over four trees, and no command, seed term or output form is named; §6's own history shows a `git grep review_converge_on -- skills/` found the sixth instance the fifth draft had missed, so the release knows a term-based seed exists and does not state one. §7 then carries rows for the five illustrative items only, so any assertion the sweep turns up outside those five is edited with no guard and no row — which is how items 1-3 got their coordinated-edit warning in the first place. The task can be closed with a sentence and nothing can contradict it.
suggestion: Give the sweep a seed and an artifact: the grep terms to run (at least `review_converge_on`, `audit_converge_on`, `non-PASS`, `consecutive_clean`, `clean flag`, `workflow field`) over the four named trees, and require the task's closure to list every hit with its disposition (rewritten / already true under both values). Add one §7 row asserting the four trees hold no surviving occurrence of the seed sentence's distinguishing phrase, so a missed instance reddens something.

finding: Row 21 carries two assertions of different kinds under one mutant. The first is behavioural (ComputeAuditDivergence emits no object on a round clean and converged under blocking while holding non-spec-coverage rows); the second is a source-text assertion (its comment no longer calls condition 4 redundant). The named mutant, 'delete condition 4', reddens the first and cannot touch the second — deleting the condition does not change the comment, and rewriting the comment does not change behaviour. Nor does the row name the mechanism for the second: the docs-contract guard reads repository documents (readRepoDoc), and §6 item 5's subject is a Go doc comment in internal/engine/divergence.go, which no guard in this release is said to read. Row 20 does name its mechanism ('the guard extension is part of the work'); row 21 does not, and the two are the same shape.
suggestion: Split row 21 into 21a (behaviour, mutant: delete condition 4) and 21b (the comment, mutant: restore the word 'redundant'), and say what reads the comment — either extend the docs-contract guard to internal/engine/divergence.go's source text, or state that item 5's comment is a deliberately unguarded edit.

finding: §2's table now decides both changed next_action branches — this closes round 11's critical — but §7 pins only one of them. Row 10 asserts 'a converged round holding non-PASS rows yields a next_action containing the count', which is the table's second row. The first row, 'clean, not yet converged', gets 'run the next audit round, and name the accepted count' in the table and no row anywhere. That branch is the one §2 says the field is for: at audit_clean_rounds 2, blocking's first clean round is not converged, so it is the round on which an operator first learns a round closed over open rows. Checked against the code, the two branches are genuinely separate — internal/engine/nextaction.go:76 dispatches converged first, then latestRoundHasFindings, then the default — so an implementation that adds the count to the converged branch alone ships with row 10 green and the branch the release exists for unchanged.
suggestion: Add a row: under blocking, at audit_clean_rounds 2, a first clean round holding warning/info rows yields a next_action that names the next round AND contains the count as a numeral; mutant — add the count to the converged branch only.

finding: Row 15's mutant is an implementation §4 says cannot exist on this command. The mutant is 'gate emission on the round's cleanliness', but cleanliness is a function of the resolved policy and §4 states at length that --merge has no access to one: engine.ResolveWorkflow reaches the task-override layer only through a spec path, --merge takes NDJSON inputs and rejects a spec-looking positional at entry (internal/cli/audit_merge.go:32 carries that refusal), and §4 rejects the active pointer as a substitute. So the mutant either cannot be written, or it is written as 'emit only when at least one row is non-PASS' — which is §4's own stated rule, not a mutation of it. Either way the row has no input that reddens it, and the trailing clause ('which empties the two buckets row 17 counts') describes an effect that gating emission does not have — omitting the object does not empty its buckets.
suggestion: Replace the mutant with one buildable on this command and observably wrong: 'emit by_severity only when the merged set holds a row whose severity is error' — which is absent on exactly the advisory-only round §4 exists for, and which row 15's all/blocking clause cannot catch since neither value reaches --merge.

finding: §2 decides that an unrecognised severity is 'Not rejected, not ignored' but treated as blocking, and the decision is right; what it does not say is that the very loop it lands in already rejects an out-of-enum value on the same row. internal/cli/audit_record.go's countAuditFindings runs invalidCategoryRows.observe on every row and returns an error — a hard refusal of the whole file — when a row's `category` is outside its enum, with a doc comment arguing that rejecting rather than warning is what the auditor prompt promises. An implementer adding severity grading to that same walk has a precedent two lines away pointing the other way, and §2's normative sentence (written because 'two earlier drafts left it to be inferred and both inferred it wrong') does not mention it.
suggestion: Add one clause to §2's unrecognised-severity paragraph: severity is graded, not validated — unlike `category`, which the record sink already rejects outright — because severity is self-declared (§2's own last paragraph) and rejecting a round over it would make the audited agent's label a gate on recording.

finding: §6 was rewritten this round to stop asserting a count and owe a derivation instead, on the ground that 'the count has been one, two, three and five, and each number was falsified by the next round'. §5 item 4 still asserts one: 'Four places pin its absence there by name.' Searching the tree for nonblocking_open, the candidates that pin its absence on the audit side are spec/0.31.0.md §8.4, spec/0.31.0.md's test list item 18, internal/cli/harness_note_test.go:263, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:641's 'review-only' parenthesis, and spec/0.31.0.tasks.json's closed_reason for the nonblocking-open task — five or six depending on whether a spec file and a closed_reason count as places, and the number is carried over from spec/0.46.0.md §8.3 rather than derived here. The clause that follows it, 'none of the four reaches it', is the load-bearing half and does not need the numeral.
suggestion: Drop the numeral: 'Several shipped documents and one guard pin its absence on the audit side by name; §4's --merge breakdown is a different surface and none of them reaches it.'

finding: Half of row 2 is green before any code is written and cannot be reddened by its own mutant. The row asserts that 'a TP_AUDIT_CONVERGE_ON in the environment and an --audit-converge-on flag both change nothing', with the mutant 'add either layer to engine.ResolveWorkflowLayers'. The env half is real and I confirmed the shape of it — TP_REVIEW_CONVERGE_ON=blocking left the resolved review_converge_on at the task-file value on this tree. The flag half is not: tp has no such flag, and `tp audit spec.md --status --audit-converge-on=blocking` exits 2 with `unknown flag: --audit-converge-on` from cobra, so the assertion holds for any string that is not a flag and holds identically whether or not ResolveWorkflowLayers grew a flag layer. The mutant cannot be applied to that half either, since adding a layer to a resolver that takes (taskOverride, project *model.WorkflowOverride) does not create the flag the assertion passes.
suggestion: Keep the env half and state the flag half as what it actually is — a negative design decision rather than a runtime assertion: 'no --audit-converge-on flag is defined on any command', asserted over the command's registered flag set, with the mutant 'define one and wire it above the task override'.
